The two-step scheduler opens pre-filled (route /study-library/live-session/schedule/step1): adjust the title, meeting date, start/end time, recurrence, or meeting link in Step 1. 5. Continue to Step 2 to adjust batches/access and participant settings, then save — the session is updated in place. 6. You can also open the session's detail page (click the card) and start the same edit flow from there.

task: Cancel or delete a scheduled live session
content_text: Cancel a single occurrence or an entire live session series. 1. Open Live Sessions > Scheduled Live Sessions (route /study-library/live-session). 2. Find the session in the 'Live' or 'Upcoming' tab. 3. Click the three-dot (…) menu on the session card and choose 'Delete Live Session'. 4. In the 'Delete Session' dialog: for a recurring session, pick 'Delete only this schedule' (one occurrence) or 'Delete entire session (all schedules)'. 5. Tick or untick 'Notify learners about the cancellation' — when unchecked, no cancellation email is sent to enrolled learners. 6. Click 'Delete' to confirm.

task: Release assessment results to learners
content_text: Make evaluated assessment results visible to learners. 1. Open Assessments and Tests > Scheduled Tests (route /assessment/assessment-list). 2. Find the assessment (usually under the 'Previous' tab for ended tests) and open it. 3. On the assessment details page, open the 'Submissions' tab. 4. Stay on the 'Attempted' sub-tab. 5. To release for one learner: click the three-dot (…) menu on their row and choose 'Release Result', then confirm in the 'Release Result' dialog. 6. To release for several learners: tick their checkboxes and choose 'Release Result' from the bulk-actions menu. 7. To release for everyone at once: use the 'Release Result' button at the top of the Attempted list ('Release Result For All Learners').

task: Allow a learner to re-attempt an assessment
content_text: Re-open an assessment for a learner who has already attempted it. 1. Open Assessments and Tests > Scheduled Tests (route /assessment/assessment-list) and open the assessment. 2. Go to the 'Submissions' tab, 'Attempted' sub-tab. 3. Click the three-dot (…) menu on the learner's row. 4. Choose 'Provide Reattempt'. 5. Confirm with 'Yes' in the 'Provide Reattempt' dialog — the learner can now attempt the assessment again. 6. For multiple learners, tick their checkboxes and choose 'Provide Reattempt' from the bulk-actions menu.

task: Copy or move a chapter to another course or module
content_text: Duplicate a chapter into (or move it to) any course/module in your institute. 1. Open Courses (route /study-library/courses) and click 'View Course' on the course. 2. In the course structure, open the Subject and Module that contain the chapter. 3. Click the three-dot (…) menu on the chapter card. 4. Choose 'Copy to' (keeps the original) or 'Move to' (removes it from the current module). 5. In the dialog, pick the destination Course, Session, Level, Subject, and Module. 6. Click 'Copy' (or 'Move') — a success toast confirms the chapter was copied/moved. Note: the same menu also has 'Edit Chapter Details' and 'Delete'.

task: Reorder, delete, or unpublish a slide in a chapter
content_text: Manage the slides inside a chapter from the slides view. 1. Open Courses > 'View Course' > expand Subject and Module > click the chapter to open its slides view. 2. Reorder: in the left slide list, grab a slide's drag handle and drag it to its new position — the order saves automatically. 3. Delete / copy / move: click the three-dot (…) menu on a slide in the list and choose 'Delete', 'Copy to', 'Move to', or 'Drip Conditions'. 4. Unpublish: select the slide, then click the 'Unpublish' button in the top toolbar and confirm 'Unpublish this slide?' — learners can no longer see it, but your content is kept. 5. Re-publish anytime with the 'Publish' button (drafts also have 'Save Draft' to save without publishing).

task: Delete a course
content_text: Permanently delete a course from the institute. 1. Open Courses (route /study-library/courses). 2. Stay on the 'All Courses' tab and find the course card (use search or filters if needed). 3. Click the red trash icon on the course card (visible to admins only). 4. In the confirmation dialog — 'Are you sure you want to delete this course? This action cannot be undone.' — click 'Confirm'. 5. The course and its enrollment structure are removed; there is no archive or undo, so consider unpublishing content instead if you may need it later.

task: Preview a course as a learner would see it
content_text: Switch the content editor into Learner View to see exactly what an enrolled learner sees. 1. Open Courses > 'View Course' on the course. 2. Expand a Subject and Module, then click a chapter to open its slides view. 3. At the top of the left sidebar, use the toggle switch labelled 'Switch to Learner View' (icons: gear = instructor, eye = learner). 4. With the toggle on, editing controls are hidden and only published slides render — the learner's experience. 5. Toggle back ('Switch to Instructor View') to resume editing. Note: unpublished/draft slides do not appear in Learner View, which is the quickest way to check what is actually live.

task: First-week setup checklist for a new institute
content_text: Recommended order for setting up a new institute in its first week. 1. Branding: on the Dashboard (/dashboard) click 'Edit Institute' to set your logo, institute details, and theme colour. 2. Naming: go to Settings > 'Naming Settings' and rename platform terms to your vocabulary (Course, Level, Session, Batch, Learner… each with singular + plural), then 'Save Changes'. 3. Create your first course: Courses (/study-library/courses) > 'Create Course' — do this before sessions, since the Sessions page requires at least one course. 4. Academic session: Manage Institute > Session (/manage-institute/sessions) > 'Add New Session' and attach courses/levels; the resulting batches (course + level + session) appear under Manage Institute > Batches (/manage-institute/batches), each with its own invite code. 5. Enroll learners: from the learner list (/manage-students/students-list) use 'Enroll in Bulk' (CSV) for existing rosters, or 'Enroll Learner' on a batch card for one-by-one enrollment; you can also share the batch invite link for self-enrollment. 6. Payments: in Settings open 'Payment Gateways' to connect your gateway and 'Payment Settings' for payment behaviour; build fee plans under Fee Management > Create Fee Plan (/financial-management/fee-plans). 7. Invite your team: Manage Institute > Teams (/manage-institute/teams) > 'Invite Users', assigning each person a role. 8. Finally, send learners their logins with the 'Share Credentials' bulk action on the learner list.

task: Understand Course vs Level vs Academic Session vs Batch vs Package
content_text: How Vacademy structures enrollment. A Course (called 'Package' in APIs and some admin screens) is the content container — subjects, modules, chapters, and slides live inside it. A Level is a stage or tier within a course, such as 'Year 1', 'Basic', or 'Advanced'; simple courses often use a single default level. An Academic Session is a time period like '2026-27' — the same course can run across many sessions. A Batch is the combination of one Course + one Level + one Academic Session, and it is the thing learners actually enroll into: enrollment counts, invite codes, live-session targeting, fee assignment, and reports all attach to batches. You manage batches at Manage Institute > Batches and academic sessions at Manage Institute > Session. Note that a live-session 'Session' (a scheduled class) is unrelated to an Academic Session, and every one of these words can be renamed per institute in Settings > Naming Settings — so your institute may show different labels for the same concepts.

task: Publish your course catalogue with Product Pages
content_text: Product Pages are hosted landing pages where visitors can browse selected courses, add several to a cart, and pay in one combined checkout — share the link anywhere, including your own website. 1. Open Automations > Product Pages (route /manage-pages/product-pages). 2. Click 'New Product Page' and give it a Page Name in the 'Create Product Page' dialog. 3. In the editor, use the 'Courses' tab to attach the courses/plans to sell, 'Page Design' to style the page, 'Settings' for checkout behaviour, 'Coupons' for discount codes, and 'Custom Fields' to collect extra info from buyers. 4. Check the 'Preview' tab to see the live page. 5. Click 'Copy Link' in the editor header to copy the shareable learner-portal URL (uses your institute's custom domain when configured), or 'UTM Link' to generate a tracking link for ads. 6. Paste that URL into your website, social bios, or campaigns — buyers land on the hosted page, no coding needed.

task: How learners access the app and log in the first time
content_text: Learners use the learner portal — a separate app from this admin dashboard — at your institute's learner URL (the address embedded in your invite links; by default learner.vacademy.io, or your custom domain if white-labelled). There are two ways in. 1. Invite link (self-enrollment): open Manage Institute > Batches (/manage-institute/batches), find the batch card, and use the copy button next to 'Invite Code' — this copies a full invite link to the learner portal; learners open it and register themselves. 2. Admin enrollment: when you enroll a learner manually ('Enroll Learner' on a batch card or from the learner list), the final step auto-generates a username and password for them. 3. To send those logins, open the learner list (/manage-students/students-list), select learners, and use the 'Share Credentials' action from the bulk-actions menu (also available per learner) — this emails them their username, password, and login link. 4. The learner signs in at the learner portal with those credentials and lands in their enrolled batch content.

task: View admin activity logs (audit trail)
content_text: See a filterable audit trail of actions taken by admins in your institute. 1. Open 'Admin Activity Logs' from the sidebar (route /admin-activity-logs). 2. If the link is missing, the feature is opt-in per institute: enable the 'Admin Activity Logs' sidebar tab in Settings > Display Settings, then reload. 3. Use the filter bar to narrow by resource/entity type, action, the admin who acted, and a date range. 4. Browse the results table (paginated). 5. Click any row to open a drawer showing the full payload of that change for inspection.

task: Set up automatic fee reminders for installments
content_text: Fee reminders are an automation that emails learners about their upcoming fee installments on a schedule you choose. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar and select the 'Automations' tab. 2. Click the 'Payments & Fees' card. 3. Next to 'Remind learners before fees are due', click 'Set up'. 4. Under 'Which message to send?', pick an email template; if you have none yet, click the 'Add sample message: "Fee Payment Reminder"' button to add a ready-made one you can edit later. 5. Under 'When should this run?', choose 'Every' 'day' or 'week' (and the weekday) and the time to send (India Standard Time). 6. Click 'Turn on automation' - the card now shows how many options are on. 7. To stop the reminders later, open the same card and switch the recipe off, then confirm with 'Turn off'. For custom recipients or conditions, use the advanced workflow builder linked at the bottom of the tab.

task: Create a fee plan with fee types and installments
content_text: A fee plan bundles one or more fee types (tuition, exam, transport, etc.) with their installment schedules and links them to classes. 1. In the sidebar, open Fee Management > Create Fee Plan. 2. Click 'Create Plan' to open the 'New Fee Plan' dialog. 3. Under 'Select Class', pick one or more classes the plan applies to, enter a 'Package Name', and set 'Status' to 'Active' or 'Draft'; turn on 'Enroll learners on approval' if enrolments should wait for admin approval. 4. Under 'When are installments due?', choose 'Fixed dates for every learner' or 'Chosen for each learner at enrollment'. 5. For each fee type, fill 'Fee Name' and 'Total Amount (₹)', and optionally tick 'Refundable' or set a 'Late Penalty' %. 6. Turn on 'Has Installments', pick a 'Payment Frequency' (Annual, Half-Yearly, Quarterly, Monthly or Custom) and check each row's Amount and Due Date until nothing is left to allocate. 7. Click 'Add Fee Type' for more fees, then click 'Save Package'.

task: Collect and record an installment payment at the counter
content_text: The Pay Installments screen is a counter-collection flow: find the learner, pick installments, record the payment and hand over the receipt. 1. In the sidebar, open Fee Management > Pay Installments. 2. Search by student name or phone and click the learner's row. 3. Use the 'All', 'Overdue', 'Due', 'Partial' and 'Paid' filters if needed, tick the installments being paid, and click 'Proceed to Pay' (or 'Generate Invoice' to issue an invoice first). 4. Under 'Payment Details', choose 'How was it paid?' (and the 'Via' option if your mode has options), and fill 'Reference' and 'Payment date' as required. 5. Enter the 'Amount' received and optional 'Remarks'. 6. Click 'Submit Payment', review the 'Confirm Payment' dialog and click 'Confirm Payment' - the amount is spread across the selected installments. 7. On the 'Payment Submitted' screen, click 'Download Receipt' or 'Pay for Another Student'.

task: Give a concession or add a penalty on a fee installment
content_text: Lower an installment with a concession (needs approval) or raise it with a penalty (applies instantly). 1. In the sidebar, open Fee Management > Pay Installments. 2. Search by student name or phone and click the learner's row. 3. In the installment list, click the pencil 'Adjust' icon on the unpaid installment. 4. In the 'Adjust Installment' dialog, choose 'Concession' (decreases the due amount) or 'Penalty' (increases it). 5. Enter the 'Amount' and a 'Reason' (e.g. Scholarship, Late payment). 6. Click 'Submit for Approval' for a concession or 'Apply Penalty' for a penalty. 7. A submitted concession shows as 'Pending' on the installment until it is approved on the Adjustment Approvals page; you can withdraw it from the same dialog with 'Retract Adjustment'.

task: Approve or reject fee concession requests
content_text: Concessions requested on installments wait here until someone approves or rejects them. 1. In the sidebar, open Fee Management > Adjustment Approvals (or click 'Adjustment approvals' on the Pay Installments or Manage Finances page). 2. Stay on the 'Pending' tab to see each request's Student, Fee Type, Type, Expected, Amount, Reason and Due Date. 3. Click 'Approve' to apply the concession to that installment, or 'Reject' to turn it down. 4. Open the 'Approved', 'Rejected' or 'All History' tab to see past decisions. 5. In the history, search by student name or phone, filter by type ('All Types', Concession or Penalty) and narrow by the 'From:' and 'To:' dates.

task: Track fee collection on the Collection Dashboard
content_text: The Collection Dashboard shows how much fee is expected, collected, due and overdue across your classes. 1. In the sidebar, open Fee Management > Collection Dashboard. 2. In the 'School Collection' header, pick a session from the 'Session -' dropdown (or 'All'). 3. Click 'Total' for all fees, or click one or more fee-type chips to see only those fees. 4. Read the summary cards: 'Projected revenue', 'Till now expected', 'Till now collected', 'Total overdue' and 'Total due'. 5. Check the 'Collection Pipeline' chart and the 'Collection Rate' gauge. 6. Use 'Class-wise Performance' to compare Projected, Expected, Collected and Collection Rate per class, and 'Payment Insights' to see collection by payment mode.

task: See each learner's fees, paid, due and overdue amounts
content_text: Manage Finances is the fee roster: one row per learner and fee plan with what was billed, paid, due and overdue. 1. In the sidebar, open Fee Management > Manage Finances. 2. Pick a session from the 'Session -' dropdown. 3. Search by name or phone, and filter by course, 'Fee Type', 'Status' (Paid, Partial, Pending, Overdue) or level; click 'Clear All' to reset. 4. Click a row to see the breakdown by fee type (Expected, Paid, Due, Overdue). 5. Click the eye icon ('View installments') to open 'Installment Details' with every installment's due date and status. 6. Click 'Collect payment' to record a payment, or 'Adjustment approvals' to review concession requests.

task: Set up offline payment modes (cash, UPI, cheque, bank transfer)
content_text: Offline payment modes are the options staff pick from when they record a payment by hand. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar and select the 'Payment Settings' tab. 2. Scroll to the 'Offline payment modes' card. 3. Turn 'Require a mode when recording a payment' on or off, and choose a 'Preselected mode' if you want one picked by default. 4. Click 'Add payment mode', type the mode name (e.g. UPI) and a reference label (e.g. UTR number), and tick 'Reference required' or 'Proof required' as needed. 5. Optionally add options under the mode with 'Add option' (e.g. PhonePe, Google Pay, or the account the money went into), and extra fields with 'Add field'. 6. To retire a mode, switch it off instead of deleting it so past payments keep pointing at it. 7. Click 'Save'.

task: Enroll a learner in several courses as one admission package
content_text: An admission package charges two or more paid courses together: one discount on the total, one installment schedule, one payment at admission and one admission receipt. 1. In the sidebar, open Manage Contacts > Linked Course Contacts and click 'Enroll Learner' (the button uses your institute's term for learners). 2. Select the learner(s) and click 'Next', then select two or more courses and click 'Next' to reach 'Enrollment Config'. 3. Turn on 'Enroll as a package' (free or subscription courses, and courses whose fee plan bills more than one fee, cannot join a package; the panel lists any such course). 4. Under 'Package discount', pick a 'Type' ('No discount', 'Flat ₹ off' or '% of total'), enter the 'Value' and 'Reason', and choose how to split it over the installments. 5. Check the 'Package installments' schedule. 6. Under 'Payment at admission', keep 'Don't record a payment now' or choose 'Record an offline payment' and enter the 'Amount'. 7. Click 'Preview', check the 'Admission package' summary, then click 'Confirm Enrollment'. 8. Later, record further payments from the learner's 'Payment History' tab with '+ Record package payment'.

task: Create a new admission and assign a fee plan
content_text: Use the admission form to admit a student - fresh, or from an existing enquiry or application - and then assign their fee plan. 1. In the sidebar, open Admissions > Admission List and pick the session in the dropdown at the top. 2. Click 'Admission Form' and, in 'Choose Admission Type', pick 'New Admission', 'From Enquiry' (click 'Search Enquiries', then 'Admit' on the right row) or 'From Application' (enter the 'Application ID / Tracking ID' or 'Phone Number' and click 'Continue'). 3. Fill the student details, including Class and Section, and click 'Save & Next' through the previous school, parent and address steps. 4. On the 'Finish' step, review the 'Admission Summary' and click 'Submit Admission'. 5. On the 'Fee Assignment' step, select the fee plan linked to the class and check its fee types and installments. 6. Optionally open 'Record payment (optional)' to capture an offline payment, then click 'Enroll with this fee plan'. 7. To find existing records, use 'Search Criteria' on the Admission List (search by Student Name, Application No or Parent Mobile).

task: Create a new application and collect the application fee
content_text: Applications sit between enquiry and admission: review applications, collect the fee, then admit. 1. In the sidebar, open Admissions > Application. 2. In 'New applications go to', choose the session, then click 'New Application'. 3. In 'Choose Application Type', pick 'New Application' or 'From Enquiry'. 4. Fill the 'Student Details', 'Academic Info' (class), 'Parent & Guardian' and 'Address' sections, using 'Next' to move on. 5. Click 'Submit Application' and confirm. 6. On the 'Payment' step, under 'Pay Now' choose 'UPI / QR Code' or 'Cash Received', fill the transaction or receipt ID, and click 'Confirm Payment'; or open 'Generate Link' to copy an 'Online Link' or 'UPI App Link', or 'Send link via Email' to the parent. 7. Click 'Back to List' - the application now appears in the list with its Tracking ID and status.

task: View the admissions report with fees, paid and due
content_text: The Admissions report shows students admitted each month with their fees, paid and due, broken down by course, source and counsellor. 1. In the sidebar, open Leads > Reports, select the 'Revenue' group and then 'Admissions'. 2. Pick a date range with the quick presets or the 'From' and 'To' dates and click 'Apply'. 3. Read the totals: 'Admissions', 'Fees', 'Paid', 'Due', 'Collected' and 'Average fee per admission'. 4. Scroll through 'Admissions by month', 'by source', 'by course group', 'by course' and 'by counsellor'; click a counsellor's row to see only their admissions ('Show all counsellors' to go back). 5. Under 'Students', click 'Show students' to list every admission with phone, email, courses, fees, paid and due. 6. Click 'Export CSV' on any section, tick the columns in 'Choose export columns', and click 'Export'.

task: Customise your lead statuses
content_text: Lead statuses are the pipeline stages a lead moves through; you can rename, recolour and add them, and pick the one new leads start in. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar and select the 'Lead Settings' tab, then stay on the 'Configuration' sub-tab (the lead cards below appear only while 'Lead Management System' is set to 'Enabled'). 2. Scroll to the 'Lead Statuses' card. 3. Type in a row's name box to rename a status, and click the colour square to change its colour. 4. Click the star on a row to make it the default status for brand-new leads. 5. Click the eye icon to hide a status from the status filter, or show it again. 6. Click 'Add status' to add a new stage, then click 'Save statuses'. Statuses can't be deleted, so leads keep their history. 7. Optionally, under 'When a lead is moved to Converted without a course', choose 'Do nothing', 'Warn first' or 'Require a course or fee plan' and click 'Save rule'.

task: Set up lead tier levels (Hot, Warm, Cold and your own)
content_text: Tier levels rank your leads (Hot / Warm / Cold by default), either automatically by score or set by hand. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar, select the 'Lead Settings' tab and stay on the 'Configuration' sub-tab ('Lead Management System' must be 'Enabled'). 2. Scroll to the 'Tier levels' card. 3. Rename a level in its name box and click the colour square to recolour it. 4. Enter a number in 'from score' so leads with at least that score land in the level automatically, or leave it blank ('manual') for a level counsellors set by hand. 5. Use 'Move up' and 'Move down' to order levels from most to least important. 6. Click 'Add Tier level' to create your own level, e.g. Super Hot. 7. Click 'Save levels'. To delete a level you added, save first and then use its delete icon; the default levels can be edited but not deleted.

task: Set a response time (TAT) and follow-up reminders for leads
content_text: Make sure new leads are contacted on time and followed up regularly; counsellors are reminded and late leads are flagged overdue. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar, select the 'Lead Settings' tab and stay on the 'Configuration' sub-tab ('Lead Management System' must be 'Enabled'). 2. In the 'Working hours' card, switch it 'On' if deadlines should follow your office hours, then pick the 'Working days' and the 'From' / 'to' times. 3. In 'New Lead Response Time (TAT)', switch it 'On' and set 'Respond to a new lead within' in hours and minutes. 4. Optionally click '+ Add an early reminder' to warn the counsellor some minutes before the deadline, and pick roles under 'Notify which roles'. 5. In 'Follow-up Reminders (SLA)', switch it 'On' and set 'Follow up again within' and the 'Early reminder'. 6. Click 'Save reminder settings'. 7. Choose the message and channel for these reminders under Settings > Automations.

task: Set up rules for duplicate leads
content_text: Decide what happens when a new lead submission matches a lead you already have. It is off by default and does not change leads already captured. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar, select the 'Lead Settings' tab and stay on the 'Configuration' sub-tab ('Lead Management System' must be 'Enabled'). 2. In the 'Deduplication' card, switch it to 'Enabled'. 3. Under 'Match leads by', choose 'Email address' or 'Phone number'. 4. Under 'Applies to', choose 'This lead list only', 'Specific lead lists' (then pick them under 'Lead lists') or 'All lead lists in this institute'. 5. Under 'When a duplicate is found', choose 'Reject the submission' or 'Allow it through and reassign'. 6. If you allow it through, use 'Repeat lead handling' to choose the counsellor ('Assign a counsellor?'), the 'Lead status', and the 'Reattempt' switches such as 'Mark the repeat as Duplicate' or 'Notify the lead's counsellor'. 7. Click 'Save deduplication settings'.

task: Merge a duplicate lead into the right person
content_text: When the same person was entered twice, an admin can merge the duplicate into the record you want to keep; the duplicate's enquiries move over and it stops counting as a lead. 1. In the sidebar, open Leads > Recent Leads. 2. Click the name of the lead you want to keep (or its 'Open details' arrow) to open the lead's details panel. 3. In the 'Duplicates' section, click 'Merge duplicate'. 4. In the search box ('Search the duplicate by name, phone or email') type at least 3 characters and pick the duplicate from the results. 5. Review the 'Keep' and 'Duplicate' columns and the list of what will change; if the two can't be merged, the reason is shown. 6. Click 'Merge' (or 'Pick someone else' to choose again). 7. To reverse it later, open the merged record and click 'Undo merge'.

task: Move leads through your pipeline on the Lead Board
content_text: The Lead Board shows your leads as cards in one column per lead status; drag a card to another column to change its status. 1. In the sidebar, open Leads > Lead Board. 2. Narrow the board with the filters at the top: tier, 'All SLA states', counsellor, audience, 'Call history', custom fields and the date range (e.g. 'Last 7 days' or 'Custom range'). 3. Type in 'Search leads across all columns' to find a lead in every column at once; click 'Clear all' to reset the filters. 4. Drag a lead card into another column to move it to that status. 5. Click a card to open the lead's details panel, where you can add notes and follow-ups. 6. Click 'Manage Column' to hide or show status columns for yourself. 7. Use 'Lead settings' to jump to the statuses setup if the board says no statuses are configured.

task: Check whether a lead is already in the system (Check Lead)
content_text: Check Lead tells you whether a phone number or email already belongs to a lead anywhere in the institute, even one assigned to a colleague. 1. In the sidebar, open Leads > Check Lead (if it says 'Check Lead is turned off', an admin can switch it on in Settings > Lead Settings > Check Lead). 2. Under 'Search by', choose 'Phone number' or 'Email address' ('Full name' appears only for counsellors when the institute allows it). 3. Enter the full value; for a phone, pick the country and type the whole number. 4. Click 'Check'. 5. If you see 'This lead is already in the system', read the details shared with you, such as 'Assigned to' and the status; a red note means the person has opted out and must not be contacted. 6. If you see 'Not in the system', click 'Add New Lead' (when available) to add them with the number or email already filled in.

task: View each counsellor's leads, activity and performance
content_text: The Counsellors page shows your counselling team with each person's assigned leads, rating and targets. 1. In the sidebar, open Leads > Counsellors (this page is off by default; if it is missing from your sidebar or says 'Counsellors page is not enabled', an admin can turn it on in Settings under 'Display Settings'). 2. Check the summary chips for 'Counsellors', 'Active' and 'Assigned leads'. 3. Use 'Search by name or email…' and the 'All' / 'Active' / 'Inactive' filter to find someone. 4. Switch between 'Cards' and 'List' views. 5. Click a counsellor's card or row to open their panel. 6. Use the panel tabs 'Leads', 'Activity', 'Calls', 'Performance' and 'Targets' ('Coaching' appears when call intelligence is on).

task: Log a note or schedule a follow-up on a lead
content_text: Record what happened with a lead and book the next follow-up from the lead's details panel. 1. In the sidebar, open Leads > Recent Leads. 2. Click the lead's name (or the 'Open details' arrow) to open the details panel. 3. Click 'Add a note or log activity…'. 4. Choose 'Note', 'Call Log', 'Follow Up' or 'Meeting'. 5. For a follow-up, pick the 'Schedule time' (required) and answer any dropdowns your institute added (those marked * are required). 6. Type your note in the text box. 7. Click 'Schedule Follow-up' (or 'Add Note' for other types). If you see 'No campaign response linked', a follow-up can't be scheduled for this lead.

task: Create a Lead Agent that finds new leads for a list
content_text: A Lead Agent finds organisations that fit what you sell and puts the best ones into a lead list every day, up to your daily limit. 1. In the sidebar, open Leads > Lead Agent (if it says 'Lead Agent is not on for your institute yet', ask your account manager). 2. Click 'New Lead Agent'. 3. In 'List & product', pick the 'Lead list' (or click 'New list'), give the agent a 'Name', fill in 'What you sell' and the 'Product description' (or click 'Suggest with AI'). 4. In 'Who to find', add 'Industries' and 'Markets' (country, plus optional state and city). 5. In 'Pace & quality', set 'Leads per day', the delivery hours and 'Days', the 'Minimum score to send', and whether to 'Approve leads before they're sent'. 6. Check the summary in 'Check & save' and click 'Save agent'. 7. The agent is saved paused; turn it on from its page with the switch and confirm 'Turn on'. Approve waiting leads in its 'Approval queue' tab.

task: Connect a calling provider so counsellors can call leads
content_text: Connect your calling service once and the call button next to each lead starts working. 1. In the sidebar, open Calling > Calling Settings (or open Settings and select the 'Calling (Telephony)' tab). 2. On the 'Provider' tab, find the 'Calling provider' card and pick your service in the 'Calling service' dropdown. 3. Paste the keys your calling service gave you into the fields shown; a saved key shows 'Saved', and leaving it blank keeps the saved one. 4. If your service offers them, set 'Which number should leads see?' and a 'Voicemail / fallback number' for callbacks nobody can take. 5. Turn on 'Record calls' if you want to play recordings back from a lead's activity timeline. 6. Make sure the switch at the top right of the card is on, then click 'Save changes'. 7. Once a service is saved, extra tabs appear for what it supports, such as 'Numbers', 'IVR menus', 'User extensions', 'Inbound setup' or 'AI calling line'; use them to add caller-ID numbers or map each counsellor to an extension. 8. Click 'Open Call Log' to check the calls your team places.

task: Call a lead from Recent Leads and log the outcome
content_text: Counsellors can call a lead in one click from the lead list; your phone rings first, then the lead is connected. 1. In the sidebar, expand Leads and click Recent Leads. 2. Find the lead, then click the phone icon next to their number in the 'Contact' column (tooltip 'Call lead'), or choose 'Call lead' from the row's menu. 3. In the 'Call from' popup, keep the number marked 'Recommended' or pick another one, then click 'Call now'. 4. Answer your phone when it rings; the lead is connected and the call status updates on screen. 5. When the call ends, a side sheet opens: pick the lead's new status (or keep the current one), add a 'Note', and optionally set a 'Next follow-up' such as 'Tomorrow 10am' or '+3 days'. 6. Click 'Save disposition', or 'Skip' if there is nothing to record. 7. If the phone icon is greyed out, hover it to see why (for example, the lead has no phone number); an admin connects calling under Calling > Calling Settings.

task: Review your team's calls in the Call Log
content_text: The Call Log lists every call across your team, AI and human, inbound and outbound. 1. In the sidebar, open Calling > Call Log (it is also under Leads > Call Log). 2. Pick a time window with the hour or day buttons, type a number in 'Last N hrs', or set 'From' and 'To' and click 'Apply' ('Reset' clears it). 3. Narrow to a team or one counsellor with the pickers on the right ('All counsellors'). 4. Read the tiles ('Total calls', 'Connected', 'Talk time', 'Unique leads', 'AI vs human') and use the 'All calls', 'Missed inbound' and 'Callbacks due' chips to jump to work that needs action. 5. Filter the table by 'Lead name', 'Number', 'Direction', 'Type', 'Status' or 'Disposition'; click a lead's name to open their profile and use the 'Recording' column to listen back. 6. Tick several calls to set 'Lead status' or 'Disposition', 'Assign counsellor' or 'Add to campaign' in one go. 7. To call someone from here, click 'Place a call', search the lead by name, phone or email (at least 3 letters), and click 'Call'. 8. If call analysis is switched on, open the 'Call Intelligence' tab for AI scores and summaries.

task: Create an AI calling agent
content_text: AI agents are the personas your AI caller speaks as; every saved agent can be used by campaigns, workflows and the IVR. 1. In the sidebar, open Calling > AI Agents. 2. Click 'New agent' to start blank, or 'From a use case' (shown as a gallery when you have no agents yet), pick a use case, answer its questions and click 'Write it with AI' or 'Use template'. 3. Under 'Persona & direction', enter the 'Agent name', choose 'Direction' ('Outbound', 'Inbound' or 'Both') and keep 'Enabled' on. 4. Under 'Voice & language', set the 'Language' and pick a 'Voice'; type a line in 'Test this voice' and play it to hear the result. 5. Under 'Script & prompt', write the 'Opening line' and the 'System prompt' (or click 'Start from a template'). 6. Under 'Goals & outcomes', list 'Questions to find out (one per line)', add 'Handoff numbers' for when a caller asks for a human, and optionally choose a booking page in 'Auto-book meetings on'. 7. Under 'After the call', add a rule for each thing the agent promises to send. 8. Under 'Test call', enter a 'Name' and 'Phone number' and click 'Save & call' to hear the agent on your own phone (a real, charged call). 9. Click 'Save agent'.

task: Start an AI call to one lead or a whole list
content_text: Let an AI agent call a lead for you; the outcome and counsellor assignment are filled in automatically after the call. 1. Make sure the robot button is turned on: in Settings > 'AI Calling', switch on 'Show the AI-call button on lead rows' and save. 2. In the sidebar, expand Leads and click Recent Leads. 3. Click the robot icon next to the lead's phone number (tooltip 'AI call lead'). 4. In the 'AI call' dialog, choose the 'AI agent' (or leave 'Default agent') and the 'Call from number' (or leave 'Auto (recommended)'). 5. Click 'Start AI call'. 6. To call a whole list, open Leads > Lead List, click the campaign card, then click 'Call all with AI'. 7. Under 'Who to call' pick only the selected leads or all eligible leads, set 'Calls at a time', and click 'Call N leads'; this uses calling credits. 8. Use 'View AI call progress', or Calling > Call Queue, to follow the run.

task: Turn on AI calling and set retries, shifts and outcome rules
content_text: AI Calling settings decide who the AI calls, how often it retries and what happens after each outcome. 1. In the sidebar, open Calling > AI Calling Settings (or open Settings and select the 'AI Calling' tab). 2. On the 'AI calling' tab, switch AI calling to 'Enabled', choose the 'AI voice provider' and fill in the 'Default Campaign ID' (the agent used when none is picked; settings cannot be saved as enabled without it). 3. Optionally switch on 'Show the AI-call button on lead rows' and 'Capture inbound callers as leads'. 4. On 'Agents & campaigns', register each campaign or agent with a friendly name and tag it 'Outbound' or 'Inbound'; click 'Add campaign' for more. 5. On 'Retries & shifts', set 'Max retries', 'Max calls per day (per lead)', 'Minutes between retries', the 'Calling shifts' (click 'Add shift' for more) and the 'Timezone'. 6. On 'Outcome → action', tick which outcomes should 'Assign counsellor' and which should 'Stop (no retry)'; use 'Add outcome' for custom ones. 7. On 'Assignment', pick the 'Assignment mode' ('Round robin', 'On-shift only' or 'Manual'). 8. Click 'Save AI calling settings' at the top; an 'Unsaved changes' tag shows until you do.

task: Create a booking page so leads can book a meeting with you
content_text: A booking page gives you a link people use to pick a free slot on your calendar. 1. In the sidebar, open Meetings > My Schedule. 2. Optionally, in the 'Your Google calendar' card, click 'Connect Google account' so meetings use your own calendar and Meet links. 3. Click 'Booking Pages', then 'New Booking Page'. 4. Under 'Basics', enter a 'Title', choose the 'Host', 'Duration' and 'Timezone', and optionally an 'Audience List (optional)' to add bookers to. 5. Under 'Availability', tick your days in 'Weekly availability' and set the hours for each, then set 'Minimum notice' and 'Booking horizon (days)'. 6. Under 'Location & Booking Rules', turn on 'Allocate Google Meet' and, if you want to approve each booking first, 'Require approval'. 7. Optionally set 'Reminders' (email or WhatsApp with an approved template, plus 'Remind before meeting') and add 'Form Questions'. 8. Click 'Create Booking Page'. 9. Share it with 'Copy booking link' from the 'Your booking links' card or the 'Booking Pages' list.

task: Schedule a meeting with a lead
content_text: Book a meeting straight from the lead's profile so it is linked to the lead. 1. In the sidebar, expand Leads and click Recent Leads. 2. Click the lead's row or name to open the side panel on the 'Lead Profile' tab. 3. In the 'Meetings' card, click 'Book meeting'. 4. In 'New Meeting', enter the 'Title', 'Date', 'Start time' and 'Duration'. 5. Check the 'Invitee (from lead)' details, which are prefilled from the lead; edit them only if they are wrong. 6. Keep 'Allocate Google Meet link' on to attach a Meet link automatically. 7. Click 'Schedule Meeting'; it then shows in the lead's 'Meetings' card and in Meetings > My Schedule. 8. For someone who isn't a lead, use 'New Meeting' on Meetings > My Schedule and fill the invitee's email or phone.

task: Create a WhatsApp template and submit it for approval
content_text: WhatsApp only delivers business-started messages from approved templates; approval usually takes minutes and at most 24 hours. 1. In the sidebar, open Communications > WhatsApp Templates. 2. Click 'Create Template'. If you see 'Create in …' instead, your WhatsApp account is connected through a partner, so create the template there and click 'Sync Templates' to import it once approved. 3. Under 'Basics', enter a 'Template Name' (lowercase, underscores only) and choose the 'Category' and 'Language'. 4. Optionally add a 'Header' (Text, Image, Video or Document); for media, click 'Upload' to add a sample file. 5. Write the 'Body Text', use 'Add Variable' for personal details, and give each variable a sample value. 6. Optionally add a 'Footer (optional)' and up to three buttons with '+ Quick Reply', '+ URL Button' or '+ Phone'. 7. Check the 'WhatsApp Preview', then click 'Submit for Approval' (or 'Save Draft' to finish later). 8. Watch the status badge ('Pending', 'Approved' or 'Rejected'); for a rejected or draft template, click 'Edit', fix the issue and click 'Submit to Meta'.

task: Reply to WhatsApp conversations in the inbox
content_text: The WhatsApp Inbox is where you read and answer WhatsApp messages from leads and learners. 1. In the sidebar, open Communications > WhatsApp Inbox. 2. Find a chat with 'Search by phone or name...', or use the 'All', 'Unanswered' (handed over by the chatbot) and 'Not delivered' filters. 3. Click a conversation to open it; a 'Waiting for your reply' note explains why the chatbot handed it over. 4. Type in 'Type a message...' and press Enter or click the send button. 5. If you see 'The 24-hour reply window has closed.', click the template icon (tooltip 'Send template (for messages outside 24hr window)'), then search and pick an approved template. 6. In 'Send template', complete 'Fill in the values' and click 'Send template'. 7. Click the refresh icon at the top (tooltip 'Refresh') to load new messages.

task: Connect your WhatsApp Business account
content_text: Connect a WhatsApp Business account so templates, workflows, chatbots and the inbox can send and receive messages. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar and select the 'WhatsApp Settings' tab. 2. Optionally use the 'Client setup guide' card ('Preview' or 'Download PDF') to see everything you need from Meta before you start. 3. On the card for the provider you use, click 'Configure' (or 'Edit' if it is already configured). 4. Enter the details asked for under 'Provider Credentials' and click 'Save Credentials'. 5. Click the round selector on that card to make it the active provider; the 'Active Provider:' banner confirms it. 6. In 'Webhook Setup', click the setup button ('Setup Webhook with …' or 'Create Channel Mapping') so incoming messages reach your institute. 7. If a 'Webhook URL' is shown for manual setup, copy it and paste it into your provider's dashboard. 8. Click 'Verify Endpoint' to confirm the connection works.

task: Build an automated workflow
content_text: Workflows run actions such as messages or AI calls automatically when something happens or on a schedule. 1. In the sidebar, open Automations > Workflows and click 'Create Workflow'. 2. Describe what you want under 'Describe your automation' and click 'Draft with AI', or set it up manually by entering a 'Workflow Name' and clicking 'Next: Choose Trigger Type'. 3. Choose 'When something happens' or 'On a schedule', then click Next. 4. For an event, pick it in 'Select Event' and optionally limit its scope; for a schedule, choose how often and when it runs. Click 'Next: Build Workflow'. 5. Pick a ready-made template with 'Use this template', or click 'Build from scratch' to open the visual editor. 6. In the editor, drag nodes from the 'Add Nodes' palette, connect them, and click a node to configure it. 7. Click 'Test Run' to do a dry run. 8. Click 'Save Draft' to keep working later, or 'Publish' to make the workflow live.

task: Open and use the assistant from any page
content_text: The assistant answers how-to questions and looks up your institute's data from any page in the admin portal. 1. On any page, click the round sparkle button at the bottom right of the screen (its tooltip reads 'Ask' followed by your institute's chatbot name); on wider screens you can also click 'Assist' on the right-side rail. 2. On the Dashboard you can instead type your question in the 'What would you like to get done today?' box and click 'Ask assistant', or click 'Open chat'. 3. In the empty panel, check the list of what you can ask (for example 'How-to guidance', 'Fees & payments' or 'Class schedules') and click a suggested question, or type in 'Ask the assistant…' and press send. 4. If an answer contains a link to a page, click it to go straight there. 5. If the assistant proposes a change (such as extending a learner's access or sending an announcement), read the 'Confirm this change' card and click 'Confirm' to apply it or 'Cancel' to skip it. 6. When a learner is open in a side view, the panel shows 'Asking about:' with their name; click the x next to it to ask about something else. 7. Use the expand icon to widen the panel, the circular-arrow icon to start a new chat, and X to close it. 8. If you don't see the button, the assistant is not turned on for your role; an admin chooses its tools in Settings under the 'AI access' tab.

task: Connect Claude, ChatGPT or another AI app to your institute (MCP server)
content_text: Let your team use their own AI apps with your institute's data; each person signs in with their own account and only sees what they can already see. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar and select the 'AI access' tab. 2. In 'Connected AI apps', under 'Enable the MCP server', switch on 'MCP server enabled'. 3. Under 'What AI can do', set each area in the 'AI apps' column to 'Off', 'View' or 'Edit', or use 'View only' or 'Turn everything on' above the list; open a row to see exactly what it allows. 4. Under 'Who can connect', use 'Add a role…' to choose which roles may connect (learners and parents can never connect). 5. Optionally, pick a role under 'Settings for' and switch on 'Customize AI apps for this role' to give it extra capabilities. 6. Click 'Save settings'. 7. In 'Connect your AI app', click 'Copy' next to 'Server URL' and share it with the people you allowed. 8. In Claude, open Settings > Connectors > Add custom connector and paste the server URL; if an app asks for a client ID, paste 'Your client ID' (use 'Add a client ID for another app' to create one for a different app). 9. The person signs in to their account and approves the connection; it then appears under 'Active connections'.

task: Add or remove members of your Sub-Org team (Sub-Org admins)
content_text: As a Sub-Org admin you manage your own team's members (the page uses your institute's name for Sub-Orgs). 1. In the sidebar, open Manage Institute > Sub-Org Teams. 2. If you look after more than one Sub-Org, pick the right one from the 'Switch sub-org' dropdown. 3. Open the 'Team' tab to see 'Team members' under 'Active' and 'Invited'; search by name, email or phone, or filter by 'Role'. 4. Click 'Add Member', enter 'Full Name', 'Email' and optionally 'Phone', and choose a 'Role' (or '+ Custom Role'). 5. Under 'User Access Mapping', select the package sessions the member should reach, then click 'Add Member'. 6. To remove someone, click the remove icon on their row ('Remove from' your Sub-Org), choose 'Remove now' or 'Keep until date' with a 'Last access date', and click 'Remove'. 7. If the page says you have no access, ask your institute admin to grant you Sub-Org admin access.

task: Add custom fields to learner profiles and enrollment
content_text: Collect extra details about your learners, such as a parent's name or a roll number. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar and select the 'Custom Fields' tab. 2. Click 'Add Custom Field'. 3. Enter a 'Field Name' and pick a 'Field Type' (for example 'Text Field', 'Dropdown', 'Date', 'Phone Number' or 'File Upload'); for dropdowns and radio buttons, fill in the 'Initial Options'. 4. Switch 'Required Field' on if it must be filled in. 5. Under 'Where should this field appear?', tick 'Learner's List', 'Learner's Enrollment' and/or 'Learner Profile', then click 'Add Field'. 6. In the 'Institute Fields' table, adjust where each field shows, whether it is 'Required', and drag rows to reorder; tick fields and click 'Add Group' to group them. 7. Under 'System Fields', you can rename built-in fields in 'Display Name' or hide them with the 'Visibility' switch. 8. Click 'Save' to keep your changes.

task: Set up a classroom panel or smart TV in a room
content_text: Pair a classroom panel (smart TV or interactive board) with a room so teachers can sign in on it; only institute admins can manage panels. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar and select the 'Classroom Panels' tab. 2. Optional: in the 'Rooms' card, click 'Add room' to add one room, or 'Paste a list' to add many (one room name per line). 3. On the panel, open the Classroom app; it shows a setup code and a number. 4. Back in Settings, click 'Add a panel' in the 'Panels' card (or 'Add a panel' on a room's row), type the 'Setup code' and click 'Continue'. 5. Pick the 'Room' for this panel, or click 'Add a new room instead' and type a 'New room name'. 6. Under 'Number shown on the panel', tap the same number you see on the panel, then click 'Pair panel'. 7. Tap Confirm on the panel; the room then shows as ready and teachers can sign in. 8. In the 'Panels' list you can see who is signed in, turn password sign-in on or off, and use the row's actions to 'Move to another room', 'End session' or 'Remove panel'.

task: Make a test look like a real computer-based exam (exam interface)
content_text: Choose how the test screen looks for learners so practice feels like the real computer-based exam. 1. Create a new assessment (or open an existing one to edit) and stay on the 'Basic Information' step. 2. Scroll to the 'Exam interface' card. 3. In 'Test screen style', pick 'Standard' or an exam style such as 'JEE Main style (web mock layout)', 'JEE Main style (console layout)', 'JEE Advanced style', 'GATE style' or 'Railway JE (RRB) style'. 4. For an exam style, turn 'Strict saving like the real exam' on if an answer should count only after the learner presses Save & Next; leave it off for practice-friendly saving. 5. For the GATE style, choose whether to show the 'On-screen calculator'. 6. On the standard screen you can instead turn on 'Show passage beside the question' for passage questions. 7. Click 'Next' (or 'Update') to save. To preview, open the test from a learner account. The picker is not available in OMR sheet mode or when a teacher checks the answers, and it is not shown for surveys.

task: Customise the learner home page
content_text: Choose what learners see first when they open the app, and in what order. This page is for institute admins and appears in the sidebar when the Learner home module is switched on for your institute. 1. In the sidebar, open 'Learner home'. 2. The first time, pick a starting point ('Start from my current home', 'Courses only', 'Classroom' or 'Storefront') and click 'Use this'; nothing changes for learners until you publish. 3. In the 'Blocks' list, drag blocks to reorder them and use the 'Shown' switch to hide or show a block. 4. Click 'Add block' to add a new block (Banner, Shortcuts, Course shelf, Notice or Event) or one of the 'Built-in widgets'. 5. Select a block to edit its 'Content', 'Who sees it', 'When' and 'Where'. 6. Check the 'Preview' on 'Phone' and 'Desktop'; use 'Preview as' to see it as particular batches or learner tags. 7. Click 'Publish', review the 'Publish learner home' checklist and click 'Publish now'; learners see it within about a minute. 8. Use 'Versions' to see earlier versions, or 'Discard draft' to drop unpublished changes.

task: Choose the learner app skin and look
content_text: Pick how the learner app looks; these choices change only what learners see, not the admin dashboard. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar and select the 'Appearance' tab. 2. Scroll to 'Learner app appearance'. 3. Under 'Theme skin', click a skin card: 'Default', 'Vibrant', 'Play', 'Cleaner Play', 'Corporate' or 'Fun'. Each card shows the learner home in your brand colour. 4. Use the preview beside the cards and switch 'Screen to preview' between 'Home', 'Lesson' and 'Quiz result'. 5. Optionally set 'Corner style' (Sharp, Rounded, Soft), 'Density' (Compact, Default, Comfortable) and 'Surface style' (Flat, Subtle, Full). 6. Click 'Save theme'. Note: with the 'Fun' skin, older app versions show Cleaner Play until learners update.

task: Add a discussion forum slide to a chapter
content_text: Ask learners a question inside a chapter and let them reply and support each other. 1. Open the chapter and click 'Add Slide'. 2. Choose 'Discussion'; a new discussion slide is added to the chapter. 3. On the 'Question & settings' tab, write the 'Question' learners will answer. 4. Under 'Who can see replies', choose 'Everyone in the batch', 'After they post their own reply' or 'Only teachers — private reflection'. 5. Turn on the options you want, such as 'Allow comments on classmates’ replies', 'Allow emoji reactions', 'Allow anonymous posting', 'Teacher approves posts before others see them' or 'Lock discussion'; optionally add a 'Care note'. 6. Click 'Save Draft' or 'Publish'; learners can't see the discussion until you publish. 7. Open the 'Responses' tab to read replies, filter by batch, and reply with 'Post as teacher'.

task: Add a Spreadsheet & Written Response question to a quiz
content_text: Ask learners to answer in a spreadsheet or written document beside a case study; answers are marked by AI against your solution. 1. Open a Quiz (or Document + Quiz) slide and, in 'Quiz Questions', click 'Add Question' > 'Add Manually'. 2. Under 'Computer-based exam (CBE)', choose 'Spreadsheet & Written Response'. 3. Optionally write the 'Scenario (shown on the left)', then write the 'Requirements'. 4. Under 'Answer parts', click 'Add spreadsheet part' or 'Add document part', and give each part a 'Label' and 'Marks'. 5. For each part, fill the 'Starting template' (for spreadsheets you can 'Import .xlsx'), the 'Solution' (or 'Import solution .xlsx') and the 'Marking scheme' lines. 6. Optionally add 'Grading notes' for the AI marker; learners never see them. 7. Click 'Add Question'. In an assessment, the same type is offered when you choose 'Create Manually' in a section; it can't be used in surveys.

task: Release course content on a schedule (drip)
content_text: Release chapters, modules or slides day by day instead of all at once. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar, select the 'Course Settings' tab and turn on the 'Drip Conditions' switch. 2. Optionally set the 'Default schedule' that every course starts from, then click 'Save Changes'. 3. Open the course from Courses in the sidebar and click 'Schedule Unlock' (this button appears once drip conditions are on). 4. In 'Schedule day-wise unlock', choose what to 'Release one' of (Subject, Module, Chapter or Slide) and set 'Every … days' and 'First one opens on day'. 5. Set 'Counted from' ('Each learner's enrollment date' or 'The batch start date') and the time it 'Opens at'. 6. Under 'Until then', choose 'Show locked' or 'Hide completely', check the day-by-day preview, and click 'Apply schedule'. 7. To undo, open 'Schedule Unlock' again and click 'Clear schedule'. Rules that depend on learner progress apply only when 'Apply progress rules to learners' is on in Course Settings.

task: Duplicate a course
content_text: Make an editable copy of a course in one step. 1. In the sidebar, open Courses. 2. On the course's card, click the duplicate icon (tooltip 'Duplicate Course'), or open the course and click 'Duplicate Course' at the top. 3. In the 'Duplicate Course' dialog, check the 'New Course name' (it defaults to the name plus '(Copy)'). 4. Review 'What is copied' (course details, the same batches, and all content as a separate copy) and 'What is not copied' (learners and enrolments, payment options, invite links, issued certificates and assigned teachers). 5. Click 'Duplicate' and keep the window open while it copies. 6. When it says the copy is ready, click 'Open new course'. The new course is not in the catalogue until you publish it.

task: Add a product to the shop
content_text: Add something your shop sells, with photos, variants and price. These screens are available when Commerce is enabled for your institute. 1. In the sidebar, open Commerce > 'Products' and click 'Add product'. 2. Under 'Details', fill the 'Name' and 'Description' on each language tab; the dot on a tab turns green when that language is complete. 3. In 'How it is sold', choose how the product is sold; this can't be changed after the product is published. 4. In 'Options and variants', set the 'Price (₹, with tax)', 'MRP (₹)' and 'SKU', or click 'Add an option' (such as size or colour), tick the values and click 'Make variants'. 5. Under 'Tax', choose a 'Tax class' (needed to publish if the shop is GST-registered), and under 'Organise' add the 'Category and collections'. 6. Click 'Save draft', then under 'Photos' click 'Upload photos'; the first photo is the cover. 7. Click 'Publish' to put it on sale. If anything is missing, the editor lists it under 'Fix these before publishing'.

task: Create an email template
content_text: Email templates are the messages used by announcements, automations (such as fee reminders) and bulk emails. 1. Open Settings from the sidebar and select the 'Template Settings' tab. 2. Stay on the 'Email Templates' tab and click 'Create Template'. 3. In the editor, click the name at the top ('Untitled Template') to rename it. 4. Fill in the 'Subject:', choose a 'Category:' (Utility, Marketing or Transactional) and optionally add 'Preview:' text shown in the inbox before the email is opened. 5. Build the email in the editor by adding and editing content blocks; use 'Assets' to add images from your library. 6. To personalise it, click a text block, then click '{ } Dynamic Values' and pick a value such as the learner's name. 7. Click 'Save Template'. 8. Back on the 'Email Templates' list, use 'Search templates...' to find it, and the row icons to preview, edit or delete it.

task: What engagement engines are and how to set one up
content_text: An engagement engine is an AI assistant with one goal (for example re-engaging quiet learners): it decides who to contact, when and what to say, and you approve the messages. 1. In the sidebar, open Engagement Engines > Engines and click 'New engine' (or 'Create your first engine'). 2. Audience: tick the batches and lead lists it should reach. 3. Basics: enter the 'Engine name', a short 'Objective' and 'The brief' (the AI's instructions; 'Generate with AI' can draft it), and pick the language. 4. Data points: choose what the AI may read for each person, such as attendance or fee dues. 5. Channels: turn on Email, WhatsApp, In-app or AI call. 6. Assets (optional): material it can send on WhatsApp. 7. Timing: set how often to reach each person, the send time, days and quiet hours. 8. Review and click 'Create engine'. It starts as a Draft and sends nothing. 9. On the engine page click 'Add people now', approve WhatsApp templates if used, then 'Start dry run' or 'Activate'. 10. Review drafted messages in Engagement Engines > Task Inbox with 'Review & send' or 'Skip'.

task: Create a WhatsApp chatbot flow and choose its provider
content_text: Chatbot Flows are automated WhatsApp conversations: when a message matches a flow's trigger, the bot replies, asks questions, saves answers and can hand over to a person. 1. In the sidebar, open Automations > Chatbot Flows and click 'New Flow'. 2. Type the flow name at the top left. 3. In the provider dropdown next to it, pick the WhatsApp provider your institute's number is connected through: 'COMBOT' (the default), 'Meta Direct' (your own Meta WhatsApp Business connection), 'WATI', or 'All Providers' to answer messages arriving through any connected provider. A flow set to one provider is matched first for that provider's messages. 4. Add steps from the 'Add Nodes' panel (Trigger, Send Message, Send Template, Send Interactive, Condition, Delay, AI Response, Ask & Save Field, Save Lead to CRM and more), connect them, and click a node to configure it. 5. Click 'Settings' to choose who is alerted when the bot hands a chat to a human. 6. Click 'Save', then 'Activate'. To edit a live flow, click 'Deactivate' first. The list page also has 'Sessions & Analytics', 'Duplicate' and 'Archive'.

task: Use Mentorship and Mentorship Settings
content_text: Mentorship pairs learners with mentors from your team for 1:1 sessions. The 'Mentorship Settings' tab in Settings only controls the notifications for it. 1. The Mentorship sidebar section is off by default; an admin can turn it on in Settings > Display Settings. 2. Open Mentorship > Mentors and click 'Add mentor': pick someone 'From your team' or use 'Invite by email'. Mentors get the Mentor role. 3. Use the assign button on a mentor's row to give them students, or 'Bulk assign' to spread many students across mentors. 4. Click 'Schedule 1:1' to book a session; track them under Mentorship > Sessions. 5. Mentorship > Requests lists learners who asked for a mentor; click 'Approve' or 'Decline'. 6. Mentors use Mentorship > My Mentorship for their mentees, availability and booking link, and can connect Google Calendar. 7. In Settings > 'Mentorship Settings', choose who is notified and on which channels (Email, In-app alert, Push notification, WhatsApp) for Mentor Assigned, Mentor Request, Session Booked, Session Cancelled, Session Reminder and Check-in Nudge, then click 'Save changes'.

task: What the Membership section offers (payments, expiry, enrollment stats)
content_text: The Membership sidebar section groups four pages for paid memberships and enrolments. 1. Payment Dashboard (/payment-dashboard): a payment overview of money collected, still owed and on its way, compared with the previous period. 2. Manage Payments (/manage-payments): every payment record and the learners who owe money, with filters and export. 3. Manage Expiry (/membership-expiry): memberships 'Recently Expired (30d)' and 'Expiring Soon (30d)', with plan end date, auto-renewal and re-enrollment rules per member, and 'Export CSV'. 4. Invite Stats (/membership-stats, page title 'Enrollment Stats'): how many people enrolled in a period. It shows Total users split into 'New' (first enrolment in that period) and 'Retainer' (already had an active enrolment before it), for Last 24 Hours, Last 7 Days and Last 30 Days, plus a 'Weekly User Trends' chart. Use the Filters (quick ranges, 'Filter by Course/Session', Start/End Date, 'User Type'), then 'View Members' to see the matching list with Joined On and Roles. Teachers do not see this section by default.

task: Increase a learner or seat limit
content_text: The admin dashboard has no setting for an overall learner count; the limits you can change are seat limits on a batch or on a sub-org. 1. To see them, open Manage Institute > Institute Overview: the 'Seats' card lists active batches with a seat limit and those almost full. 2. To raise a batch's limit, open Manage Institute > Inventory Management (/manage-inventory), find the batch and click 'Capacity'. 3. In 'Update Capacity', either switch on 'Unlimited Capacity' or enter a higher 'Maximum Seats'. 'Available Slots (Override)' is optional; leave it empty to calculate from current enrolments. 4. Click 'Save Changes'. 5. For a sub-org, open Manage Institute > Manage Institute Sub-Orgs, open the sub-org, click 'Edit' and raise its 'Seat cap'. That page is off by default; an admin can show it in Settings > Display Settings. If a limit message is not about a batch or sub-org seat limit, it comes from your institute's plan: contact your account manager or support.

task: How teachers and instructors log in after being invited
content_text: Teachers, instructors and other team members sign in to this same admin dashboard (not the learner app). 1. An admin invites them: Dashboard > 'Manage Users' > 'Invite Users', or Manage Institute > Teams. 2. The invite email has a login link and, for a new account, a username and password. The link goes to your institute's own admin portal address if one is set up, otherwise to dash.vacademy.io/login. 3. On the login page they enter the 'Username' and 'Password' and click 'Login', or use 'Use Email OTP' to get a 6-digit code instead. 'Forgot Password?' emails their login details again. 4. If they belong to more than one institute, they pick one under 'Select Your Institute' and click 'Continue to Dashboard'. 5. They see only the pages their role allows. If the email never arrived, open 'Manage Users', go to the 'Invites' tab and choose 'Resend Invite' from the person's menu. An existing account (for example in another institute) gets an email without a password and signs in with its current password.

task: Understand the Manage Payments page
content_text: Manage Payments (Membership > Manage Payments) lists every payment record and who still owes money. 1. Pick the period with the date dropdown at the top left; the line beside it sums paid, collected, need attention and abandoned. 2. The cards: 'Total' (collected plus still to collect), 'Collected' (money received), 'Outstanding' (every unpaid instalment and invoice), 'Due' (overdue on instalments, renewals and invoices), 'Upcoming' (falls due soon, not yet owed), 'Payment pending' (checkouts awaiting the gateway) and 'Failed' (online transactions declined). Click a card to filter the table; the gear button chooses which cards show. 3. The tabs above the table: 'All', 'Paid', 'Pending', 'Abandoned' (old unfinished checkouts), 'Failed', and 'Outstanding' / 'Due' / 'Upcoming', which switch to a list of learners who owe money. 4. Search by name, email, phone, amount, invoice number, plan or transaction ID; 'Filters' adds payment type, plan status, source and course. 5. Click a row for details; 'Manage Column' hides or reorders columns. 6. 'Export' downloads 'Payments (CSV)' or 'Invoices (ZIP)'.

task: Change the subject or section name in an assessment
content_text: An assessment has one Subject, chosen on the Basic Information step, and sections whose names start as 'Section 1', 'Section 2' and so on. 1. To change the subject, open the assessment in the builder and go to the 'Basic Information' step. 2. Pick another value in the 'Subject' dropdown (required). The list comes from the subjects in your courses. 3. Click 'Update' (or 'Next') to save. 4. To rename a section, go to the 'Add Questions' step, click the pencil icon next to the section name, type the new name and press Enter (Escape cancels). Click 'Update' to save. 5. To rename the subject itself, open the course in Courses, open the subject's menu, choose 'Edit Subject', change the name and click 'Save Changes'. Courses built with a 2- or 3-level structure use a built-in subject called 'DEFAULT' that does not show as a subject card in the course, so it cannot be renamed there. Pick a named subject in the assessment instead.

task: Why leads still show Pending after being attended
content_text: 'Pending' is driven by the lead's status and follow-ups, not by calls or visits on their own. Calling or meeting a lead does not change it until the status is updated. 1. In Leads > Reports > Pipeline > 'Dispositions', the 'Pending' column counts assigned leads with no status change ever recorded, meaning never worked on. Give each attended lead a status: in Leads > Recent Leads click the status chip on the lead's row and pick the new status, or select several leads and use 'Bulk actions' > 'Change status'. On the Lead Board you can drag the card to another column. 2. In Leads > Follow-ups, the 'Pending' tile counts overdue follow-ups. Close each one with 'Mark complete' on its row. 3. If your institute has a lead status named Pending (often the default for new leads), the lead stays in it until someone changes the status. Admins can rename statuses or change the default in Settings > 'Lead Settings' > 'Lead Statuses'.

task: Overview: what the Courses (LMS) section does
content_text: Open the LMS category on the sidebar's left rail. Items (some are hidden until an admin turns them on in Settings > Display Settings): - LMS Dashboard (/lms-dashboard): classes, learners, doubts and learning activity. - Learner home (/learner-home): design the learner app's home page (admin, opt-in). - Courses (/study-library/courses): browse, build, publish and duplicate courses. - Course Creation: 'Create new course from scratch', 'Create course from AI' (/study-library/ai-copilot) and Bulk Content Upload. - Live Sessions: dashboard, scheduled sessions, create new, bulk schedule, attendance and feedback. - Course Planning and Logbook: curriculum timeline planner, AI lecture planning, log course progress. - Institute Pulse (/institute-pulse): a batch's roster, content map and live feed. - Learning Reports (/study-library/reports). - Gamification and Points (/study-library/gamification). - Learning Engagement: interactive class, create engaging content, Daily Engagement (/engagement). - Doubt Management (/study-library/doubt-management). - Student AI (/study-library/student-ai). - Assessments and Tests, Questions Banks and Papers, Content Library. - Access Passes (/access-passes): bundles of courses given to pass holders.

task: Overview: what the Leads (CRM) section does
content_text: Open the CRM category on the sidebar rail and expand Leads. Some items are off by default or admin-only. - Lead List (/audience-manager/list): create and share lead campaigns and forms. - Lead Agent (/audience-manager/lead-agent): finds matching organisations and adds them to a list daily. - Recent Leads (/audience-manager/recent-leads): every lead with filters, assignment, status and bulk actions. - Lead Board (/audience-manager/lead-board): leads as cards per status; drag to move. - Follow-ups (/audience-manager/follow-ups): your Pending, Today and Upcoming follow-ups. - Call Log (/audience-manager/call-log): every call, AI and human. - Check Lead (/audience-manager/lead-lookup): see if a phone or email is already a lead. - Onboarding (/audience-manager/onboarding): who is at which onboarding step. - AI Intelligence (/audience-manager/ai-intelligence): calling quality and activity trends. - Counsellors (/counsellors): each counsellor's leads, activity and targets. - Sales Dashboard (/sales-dashboard): pipeline and counsellor performance. - Reports (/audience-manager/reports): pipeline, campaign, calling, team and revenue reports. - Campaigns (UTM): UTM attribution. - Ad Performance: Meta and Google ad spend against enquiries. - Social Posts: plan and publish social posts.

task: Overview: what the Manage Institute section does
content_text: Open the CRM category on the sidebar rail and expand Manage Institute. - Institute Overview (/manage-institute/overview): learners, courses, batches, seats and sub-orgs on one page. - Batches (/manage-institute/batches): every course + level + session batch, with invite codes, enrolment and learner lists. - Session (/manage-institute/sessions): create, edit or delete academic sessions. - Teams (/manage-institute/teams): invite staff, assign roles and build the reporting org chart. - Sub-Org Teams (/manage-suborg-teams): a sub-org admin's own team view (off by default). - Manage Institute Sub-Orgs (/manage-custom-teams): the institute's sub-organisations, their seats and details (off by default). - Inventory Management (/manage-inventory): seats and capacity per batch, including 'Unlimited Capacity'. - Manage Packages (/admin-package-management): browse and filter all packages (admins only). Labels follow your Naming Settings, so 'Batches', 'Session' or 'Sub-Org' may use your own terms. Items marked off by default can be turned on in Settings > Display Settings.

task: Overview: what the Communications section does
content_text: Open the CRM category on the sidebar rail and expand Communications. - Messaging Dashboard (/communication/dashboard): email delivery and engagement and WhatsApp volume at a glance. - In-App Messages (/chat): in-app chat conversations. - Notification Hub (/communication/notification-hub): stats, recent learner activity and inbox conversations (off by default). - WhatsApp Inbox (/communication/inbox): view and reply to WhatsApp conversations. - WhatsApp Templates (/communication/whatsapp-templates): create templates and submit them for Meta approval (with WATI, synced templates are view-only). - Create Announcement (/announcement/create): one message to in-app placements, push, email and WhatsApp, sent now, later or on repeat. - Email Campaigning (/announcement/email-campaigning): create or edit an email campaign. - Announcement History (/announcement/history): past announcements with details and delivery stats. - Schedule Announcement (/announcement/schedule): calendar of scheduled announcements. - Announcement Approval (/announcement/approval): approve announcements waiting for review. Channel setup (WhatsApp, email senders, push) lives in Settings.

task: Overview: what the Assessments section does
content_text: Open the LMS category on the sidebar rail and expand Assessments and Tests. - Assessment Dashboard (/assessment/dashboard): your tests at a glance. - Scheduled Tests (/assessment/assessment-list?selectedTab=liveTests): find, open and manage tests, release results and give reattempts. - Create Deadline Based Tests: an exam with a live start and end window. - Create anytime attempt Test: a mock test learners can take any time. - Create survey: a survey with no marks. - Test Evaluations (/evaluation/evaluations): submissions and marking. - Scanned Answer sheet Evaluation (/evaluation/evaluation-tool): mark scanned paper answer sheets. - Evalezy (/evalezy): simple scan-and-check page (off by default). Separate sidebar items: - Questions Banks and Papers (/assessment/question-papers): upload, import and manage question papers. - Content Library (/assessment/question-library): every question your institute has, organised by subject, chapter and topic, for reuse in any test. Each create option opens the builder: Basic Information, Add Questions, Add Participants, then access control and publish.

task: Overview: what the Learners (Manage Contacts) section does
content_text: Open the CRM category on the sidebar rail and expand Manage Contacts. - Contacts Dashboard (/manage-contacts/dashboard): everyone you know, learners and lead respondents, counted once per person. - All Contacts (/manage-contacts): every contact of the institute in one list. - Linked Course Contacts (/manage-students/students-list): the learner list for people enrolled in courses. Add or bulk-import learners, enrol them, view profiles and progress, record offline payments, export, and send logins with 'Share Credentials'. - User Tags (/user-tags/institute): create tags to group users ('Create New Tag'). - Link Tag (/user-tags/link): attach tags to users by user ID or 'CSV Upload'. - Invite Users (/manage-students/invite): create and share invite links so learners enrol themselves. The 'Course' and 'Invite' words follow your Naming Settings. Enrolment requests, batches and sessions live under Manage Institute.
